assumptions.name: HB-prescribed_certificate
assumptions.math: \begin{aligned}V_f(u,v)={}&c_0(f(v)-f_*)+c_1(f(u)-f_*)\\&+\sum_{i,j=1}^4Q_{ij}\langle s_i,s_j\rangle,\qquad Q\in\mathbb S^4,\qquad s_f(u,v)=\big(u-x_*,\nabla f(u),v-x_*,\nabla f(v)\big).\end{aligned}

assumptions.name: HB-L-definition
assumptions.math: \mathsf L(q,a,b)\text{ means that there exist }c_0,c_1,Q\text{ (possibly parameter-dependent), }Q\in\mathbb S^4,\ Q\text{ need not itself be positive semidefinite, with the same coefficients working for every admissible objective, dimension, and initial pair, and satisfying }w=(1+b)v-bu-a\nabla f(v),\ f(w)-f_*\le V_f(v,w)\le V_f(u,v).

assumptions.name: HB-C-definition
assumptions.math: \mathsf C(q,a,b)\text{ means that some finite dimension }d\ge1,\text{ some fixed }f\in\mathcal F_{q,1}(\mathbb R^d),\text{ and some integer }K\ge2\text{ admit a nonconstant }K\text{-periodic HB trajectory.}

assumptions.name: HB-G-definition
assumptions.math: \mathsf G(q,a,b):\quad \forall d\geq1\ \forall f\in\mathcal F_{q,1}(\mathbb R^d)\ \forall(x_{-1},x_0)\in(\mathbb R^d)^2:\ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|x_t-x_*\|=0.

main_theorem.statement_math:
**Theorem A — An exact separation witness.** At

$$
(q_*,a_*,b_*)=\left(\frac1{100},\frac{113}{50},\frac35\right),
$$

both $\neg\mathsf L(q_*,a_*,b_*)$ and $\neg\mathsf C(q_*,a_*,b_*)$ hold. The first statement excludes every coefficient choice in (L-form). The second excludes every nonconstant finite cycle, in every finite dimension, over the entire admissible function class.
main_theorem.rate: No asymptotic rate is part of Theorem A; HB-B below gives the separate uniform rate on the closed box.
main_theorem.measure: absence of a common prescribed two-point certificate and absence of nonconstant finite periodic trajectories

proof.description: Instantiate the central complex witness z,R,F,eta and four samples, then verify the exact residual certificate and diagonal zeros.
proof.produces: the four-point data satisfy every interpolation inequality

proof.description: Apply HB-INTERPOLATION to realize the data by one globally admissible objective with minimizer zero.
proof.produces: a legal fixed objective realizing the witness

proof.description: Set u=z^{-1}, v=1, and w=z; the definition of eta gives the exact Heavy-Ball successor from the state (u,v) to w.
Use the expanding similarity of the four state features.
proof.produces: feature vectors scale componentwise by z

proof.description: Multiplication by the same complex number multiplies every real inner product and both sampled value gaps by R, so every prescribed coefficient choice satisfies the printed scale identity.
proof.produces: scaled certificate equality for arbitrary c_0,c_1,Q

proof.description: Assuming (L), the monotonicity half of the certificate inequalities and the scale identity give (R-1)V_f(u,v)<=0; because R>1 this yields V_f(u,v)<=0.
proof.produces: V_f(u,v)<=0 under the assumed prescribed certificate

proof.description: Objective-gap domination at the successor gives the printed contradiction. The witness data identify the successor sample gap as F_2=FR, but the source display writes the positive term as FR.
proof.produces: F_2=FR by the witness sample values, hence neg L(q_*,a_*,b_*)

proof.description: For the cycle half, assume a finite periodic trajectory at the central parameters; this is exactly the situation ruled out by the all-frequency cycle exclusion lemma.
proof.produces: a hypothetical nonconstant finite cycle at (q_*,a_*,b_*)

proof.description: Apply the all-frequency Fourier positivity lemma as the terminal cycle argument: adding the k=-1 and k=4 lag inequalities forces every nonzero Fourier mode to vanish, so the trajectory is constant.
A constant cycle contradicts the nonconstant condition in the definition of C, proving not C in every finite dimension and period.

key_lemmas.name: HB-INTERPOLATION
key_lemmas.statement_math: I_{ij}=F_i-F_j-\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle-\frac{\|g_i-g_j\|^2+q\|x_i-x_j\|^2-2q\langle g_i-g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle}{2(1-q)}\ge0\ \text{for every ordered pair }(i,j)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \text{finite data are realizable by }f\in\mathcal F_{q,1}.
key_lemmas.role: Provides both interpolation necessity for cycles and an explicit globally admissible conjugate interpolant for finite witnesses.

proof.description: Set the shifted curvature variables and quote the smooth upper bound after subtracting q||x||^2/2.
proof.produces: ell=1-q, psi is convex and ell-smooth

proof.description: For fixed x_j subtract the linear form, define phi, and use convexity to make x_j a global minimizer.
proof.produces: varphi(x_j) is no larger than varphi at the gradient-step point

proof.description: Apply the ell-smooth descent inequality to the 1/ell gradient step from x_i.
proof.produces: the gradient-step value is bounded by varphi(x_i) minus the squared gradient difference

proof.description: Combine the two displayed gradient-step inequalities and rearrange to the cocoercive interpolation inequality.
Substitute p_i=g_i-qx_i and expand (CI) into the ordered residual condition.
Add (CI) to its reverse to obtain cocoercivity and then the ell-Lipschitz bound by Cauchy–Schwarz.
Assuming all residuals nonnegative, define p_i,h_i, the max of equal-curvature quadratics H, its conjugate, and f.
proof.math: p_i=g_i-qx_i,\quad h_i=F_i-\frac q2\|x_i\|^2,\quad H(p)=\max_i\{\langle p,x_i\rangle-h_i+\frac{\|p-p_i\|^2}{2\ell}\},\quad f(x)=H^*(x)+\frac q2\|x\|^2.

proof.description: Direct expansion gives H_i(p_i)-H_j(p_i)=I_ji>=0, so each piece is active and x_i belongs to the subdifferential at p_i.
proof.produces: H_i is active at p_i and x_i∈∂H(p_i)

proof.description: Conjugacy at active points gives H*(x_i)=h_i and ∇H*(x_i)=p_i, hence f(x_i)=F_i and ∇f(x_i)=g_i.
proof.produces: exact interpolation of values and gradients

proof.description: Each H_i minus ||p||^2/(2ell) is affine, so H is 1/ell-strongly convex; coercivity gives a unique minimizer P(x) of H(p)-<x,p> for every x.
Add the strong subgradient inequalities at P(x),P(y) to obtain monotonicity and the ell-Lipschitz estimate.
Use the two maximizing inequalities for H* to bound the differentiability remainder.
proof.produces: 0<=remainder<=ell||v||^2 and H* is differentiable with gradient P

proof.description: Add q||x||^2/2 to H*: the interpolant is q-strongly convex and has gradient Lipschitz constant at most ell+q=1.
proof.produces: f belongs to F_{q,1} globally; the Lipschitz-gradient inequality is derived from the printed bound that the gradient Lipschitz constant is at most ell+q=1

key_lemmas.statement_math: \neg\mathsf C(q_*,a_*,b_*):\text{ every finite periodic trajectory in every finite dimension is constant}.

key_lemmas.name: HB-CAUSAL-CONTINUATION
key_lemmas.statement_math: g=\|G\|,\quad m=\|M\|,\quad C_0=1+gL_0m/\eta.\qquad \text{If a solution of }x=e+G(\tau D(x))\text{ is already known to belong to }\ell_2,\text{ then}\quad 0\le-\eta\|p\|_2^2+L_0m\|p\|_2\|e\|_2,\quad p=\tau D(x).\qquad \|p\|_2\le L_0m\|e\|_2/\eta,\qquad \|x\|_2\le C_0\|e\|_2.\tag{D9}\qquad \text{These are conditional estimates so far.}\qquad \text{Bounded increasing partial energy sums establish }x\in\ell_2.\ \text{Only now apply (D9) to sharpen its gain back to }C_0.\ \text{A fixed number of steps, with an integer }J\ge\max(1,2C_0gL_0)\text{ and }\delta=1/J,\text{ reaches }\tau=1;\text{ the case }g=0\text{ is immediate. This proves stability and (D9) without any external stability theorem or uncontrolled terminal terms.}
key_lemmas.role: Establishes square summability of the actual trajectory before applying infinite-trajectory estimates.

proof.description: For a square-summable loop x=e+G(\tau D(x)), set p=\tau D(x), substitute x=e+Gp into D4, and use Parseval together with D8 to obtain the printed quadratic estimate.
Divide when p is nonzero (zero case immediate) to derive both conditional gain inequalities.

At tau=0 the solution is x=e. Assume the local homotopy induction hypothesis at the old gain tau: every ell2 input has a square-summable old-loop output satisfying D9. Choose delta with C0 delta g L0<=1/2 and proceed by homotopy.
proof.produces: old-gain continuation induction hypothesis and admissible continuation increment

proof.description: Strict causality of the loop representation defines each finite prefix of the new tau+delta solution without assuming x lies in ell2; define P_n and the truncated old-loop input r^(n), which lies in ell2.
Apply the old-gain continuation induction hypothesis to the valid input r^(n), obtaining an ell2 old-loop output y^(n); strict causality and induction over time identify prefixes P_n y^(n)=P_n x.
proof.produces: ell2 old-loop output y^(n) and prefix identity

proof.description: Record the old-loop D9 estimate for the ell2 output y^(n) with input r^(n).

Bound the truncated old-loop input by the external input plus the increment term, using r^(n)=e+delta G(P_nD(x)), the gain g=||G||, the exported pointwise bound ||D(u)||<=L0||u||, and the prefix identity P_n y^(n)=P_n x.
proof.produces: input estimate ||r^(n)||_2 <= ||e||_2 + delta g L_0||P_n x||_2

proof.description: Combine the old-loop estimate, the input estimate, and the prefix identity to obtain the first displayed inequality for ||P_n x||_2.
Absorb the increment term using the chosen side condition C0 delta g L0<=1/2 to obtain the displayed uniform partial norm bound.
Bounded increasing partial energy sums prove x is in ell2; then sharpen the gain via D9 and choose J>=max(1,2C0gL0), delta=1/J to reach tau=1.
proof.produces: actual trajectory is square summable and satisfies D9

key_lemmas.name: HB-FREE-RESPONSE-TOTAL-ENERGY
key_lemmas.statement_math: \forall(q,a,b)\in B\ \forall d\ge1\ \forall f\in\mathcal F_{q,1}(\mathbb R^d)\ \forall Y_0:\quad \sum_{t\ge0}\|Y_t\|^2\le(1+200\cdot610000^2)\|Y_0\|^2\le C\|Y_0\|^2,\qquad C=10^{14}.\tag{D10}\qquad S_t=\sum_{j=t}^\infty\|Y_j\|^2,\qquad S_t\le C\|Y_t\|^2,\qquad S_{t+1}=S_t-\|Y_t\|^2\le(1-C^{-1})S_t,\qquad\|Y_t\|^2\le C(1-C^{-1})^t\|Y_0\|^2.

proof.description: Set alpha and use endpoint comparison on the box to obtain the discriminant and root-location facts.
proof.produces: alpha>0, alpha^2>4b, and both characteristic roots lie in (0,1)

proof.description: Define the scalar impulse-response recurrence and use the root formula to get nonnegativity.
Sum the one-sign impulse response of G to obtain the exact gain bound and then combine with m<3 and D9.
Write the free response in terms of k_t.
Define R_k,R_1 and sum the recurrence and its square to obtain the two identities.
Apply Cauchy–Schwarz and endpoint comparison to bound the free-response energy by 100 times the initial energy.
Combine loop and free-response bounds for Y_t to obtain D10.
Apply D10 to every tail, define S_t, and derive tail contraction and the pointwise state estimate.
Undo translation and take square roots to print D11/Theorem B rate.

key_lemmas.name: HB-RECORD-GENERAL
key_lemmas.statement_math: \forall(q,a,b)\in\mathcal D\ \forall d\ge1,\ \text{if four samples indexed by }*,0,1,2\text{ have }(x_*,g_*,F_*)=(0,0,0),\ \text{all ordered interpolation residuals nonnegative }(I_{ij}\ge0\ \forall(i,j)),\ x_2=(1+b)x_1-bx_0-a g_1,\ S^TS=RI,\ R>1,\ x_{j+1}=Sx_j,\ g_{j+1}=Sg_j,\ F_{j+1}=RF_j\ (j=0,1),\ F_0>0,\ \text{then no common finite-valued }\Phi\text{ of the displayed full two-point oracle record }\mathcal O_f(u,v)=\big(u-x_*,\nabla f(u),v-x_*,\nabla f(v),f(u)-f_*,f(v)-f_*\big)\text{ can satisfy }f(w)-f_*\le\Phi(\mathcal O_f(v,w))\le\Phi(\mathcal O_f(u,v))\text{ for every admissible objective and every initial pair at these parameters and dimension.}

proof.description: Fix arbitrary parameters, dimension and witness; set J={*,0,1,2}, L=1-q, p_i=g_i-qx_i and h_i=F_i-q||x_i||²/2, then expand the residual to equation (1).
Record the explicit numerator identity showing the original q coefficient is retained.
Define Q_i and H on all of R^d; use Q_i(p_i)-Q_j(p_i)=I_ji>=0 to establish active pieces and the strong support inequality.

Subtracting ||p||²/(2L) leaves an affine maximum, so H is finite continuous and 1/L-strongly convex; the starred piece gives H(0)=0 and H(p)>=||p||²/(2L). Coercivity yields a unique minimizer P(x) for H(p)-<x,p>.
proof.produces: global conjugate attainment and unique P(x)

proof.description: Apply strong subgradient inequality (4) at P(x),P(y) to obtain monotonicity and the Lipschitz estimate (5).
Use maximizing inequalities for the conjugate to bound the remainder and conclude H* is globally differentiable with gradient P and L-Lipschitz gradient.
Use active pieces to identify P(x_i)=p_i and H*(x_i)=h_i, then define the base interpolant f_0.
proof.produces: base function f_0 and exact sample realization

The starred sample fixes f_0(0)=0 and gradient zero; strong convexity makes zero the unique minimizer and completes admissibility in the original dimension.

key_lemmas.name: HB-ENERGY-INFINITE
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{On the closed box, for each fixed }f,\text{ let }T_f\text{ be the centered two-state HB update and }C=10^{14}.\quad \text{For every finite }d\ge1,\text{ every admissible fixed objective }f,\text{ and every centered state }Y,\quad E_f(Y)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\|T_f^jY\|^2.\qquad \|Y\|^2\le E_f(Y)\le C\|Y\|^2,\qquad C=10^{14}.\qquad E_f(T_fY)=E_f(Y)-\|Y\|^2\le(1-C^{-1})E_f(Y).\qquad \sum_{j=N}^{\infty}\|T_f^jY\|^2\le C(1-C^{-1})^N\|Y\|^2.\qquad \text{The continuous partial sums converge uniformly on bounded sets, so }E_f\text{ is continuous.}

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{On the same box, for each fixed objective and every centered state }Y,\quad N=48C=4\,800\,000\,000\,000\,000.\qquad \mathcal E_{f,N}(Y)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|T_f^kY\|^2.\qquad \|Y\|^2\le\mathcal E_{f,N}(Y)\le C\|Y\|^2.\qquad \mathcal E_{f,N}(T_fY)-\mathcal E_{f,N}(Y)=\|T_f^NY\|^2-\|Y\|^2\le-\tfrac12\|Y\|^2.\qquad \mathcal E_{f,N}(T_fY)\le(1-1/(2C))\mathcal E_{f,N}(Y).\qquad \text{This is continuous as a finite sum of continuous compositions.}\qquad \text{Smoothness gives }f(w)-f_*\le\|w-x_*\|^2/2,\text{ so the translated }\mathcal E_{f,N}\text{ satisfies the same lower-bound and monotonicity inequalities requested of }V.
